segmentation.text: within a business or residence district
emerging or entering an alley, driveway or building
shall stop such vehicle immediately prior to
driving onto a sidewalk or onto the sidewalk area extending across any alleyway or driveway
as may be necessary to avoid collision
to all vehicles approaching on said roadway

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'The driver of' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency).

As LVMC_11_20_060_o1: st.driveway_or_alley_entrance 'private road, alley or driveway meeting the highway', st.alley 'a narrow way within a block'; a building's vehicle access is a driveway (DEF-NRS-484A-190 'every way or place in private ownership and used for vehicular travel'); the subject occupies one (rel.occupies).

The yielding accompanies driving onto the sidewalk: the duty runs while the subject occupies the sidewalk region s (st.sidewalk 'area for pedestrians between roadway and property line', whose exclusion 'a crosswalk' does not apply; rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (... sidewalk ...)'). While it waits before the sidewalk it is halted, and the stop itself is LVMC_11_20_060_o1's duty.

To yield is not to proceed in preference: kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' tells a subject still proceeding; rel.contact 'touch or overlap (a collision)' is precedence taken outright; its exclusion 'a near miss' is respected (the near conflict is bounded by the operationalizations).
'pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian (ru.aggregate 'membership of a legal aggregate'); 'any' = every member present.

operationalizations.standard: right-of-way: DEF-NRS-484A-210 'approaching under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence to the other'
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: danger of a crash where the constant-velocity closest approach of centres is below a centre clearance within a time-to-collision horizon

operationalizations.standard: as may be necessary to avoid collision
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: yielding is necessary exactly where a collision would follow under constant velocities, a closest approach below the centre clearance within the horizon

assumptions.meaning: the place of the road user at the observation lies in a business district or a residence district, as the map's reading classifies the area

applicability: asm.business_or_residence_district holds; the subject, a vehicle, occupies a driveway-or-alley-entrance region or an alley region d (st.driveway_or_alley_entrance or st.alley), and occupies a sidewalk region s (st.sidewalk).
obligation: For every road user p, other than the subject, that is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian): not (the subject's kin.speed exceeds p.halt_speed_tolerance while prim.closest_approach_within(subject, p; p.conflict_horizon) holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, p; p.conflict_horizon) below p.conflict_centre_clearance), and not rel.contact(subject, p).

narrowings.why: 'The driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion
precedence is read as the subject not proceeding while a constant-velocity closest approach to the pedestrian falls below the centre clearance within the horizon, and never touching the pedestrian

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: District assumed; the subject crosses the sidewalk out of a driveway while a pedestrian walks toward its path; the closest approach falls below the clearance within the horizon and the subject keeps moving.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same, but the subject waits halted at the sidewalk edge until the pedestrian has passed.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject travels on the roadway, nowhere near a driveway or sidewalk.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: District assumed; the subject crosses the sidewalk with a pedestrian approaching, but the subject's speed is not observed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: District assumed; the subject crosses the sidewalk out of a driveway with no other road user in the scene.

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: Hayward (1972) time-to-collision; Swedish Traffic Conflict Technique (Hydén 1987)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: passenger-car dimensions (AASHTO design vehicle P: 5.8 m by 2.1 m)

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed noise floor of vehicle odometry and tracked-object estimates
